rv.q: "Hundreds and Hundreds of Stars" also has yet to arrive at an ending; there's an abrupt finish right now to director Kimberly Senior's production that doesn't feel right, given all the unanswered questions...
While I didn’t think all elements of the material worked, this play is a good reminder that navigating the immigrant experience without making any mistakes is an impossible feat.
Competent cast notwithstanding, Senior’s direction makes “Stars” a tale of heart-wrenching urgency but it’s overcome by production bells and whistles.
It’s a moving, often humorous tale about family, immigration and American identity.
Hundreds and Hundreds of Stars succeed because it is not a lecture on immigration policy, but a human portrait drawn from it.
Delgado’s bold, endearing and powerful “Hundreds and Hundreds of Stars” lays bare how our evolving policies so completely impact one family caught up in our fraught immigration system.

Delgado, whose 2017 homage to Chicago Latine nightclub La Havana Madrid became a smash hit for Teatro Vista, has created an intimate and layered look at families caught up in the labyrinthine and deeply unfair and racist laws governing immigration.
“Hundreds and Hundreds of Stars” by Delgado is an exploration of what it means to be an American.
The World Premiere of "Hundreds and Hundreds of Stars", written by Delgado and starring Delgado as Clara is a masterful bit of storytelling...
Hundreds and Hundreds of Stars brings up questions about citizenship and the scrutinous treatment of non-citizens.

cn.t: Delgado's timely immigration drama earns praise for its political relevance and personal stakes, though some critics find it weighed down by dreamlike sequences. Strong performances anchor this important if uneven family story.
